rationale: Feature-shaped source ('consuming delegated-auth connections' from CLI agents and stdio MCP servers). Named entities: AgentREPL, agent daemon (agentd), parrot mcp-local, StdioMCPServer, Claude Code / Codex hosts, PrincipalResolver, CredentialStore, /api/v1/connections, connection.* bus, O365_PRINCIPAL, device code. Plan: orient on the CLI, local-MCP and agentd surfaces via the wiki, then read the exact seams where identity / credentials enter a CLI-run agent or a stdio MCP server, the MCP client-side OAuth machinery already in parrot.mcp (possible loopback / token storage precedent), the server-side MCP principal guard, and the recent history of those files.

queries.intent: Orient: the console CLI agents surface (AgentREPL, REPL session, permission context) in the knowledge graph.

params.question: parrot cli AgentREPL agent_repl permission context identity session

queries.intent: Orient: parrot mcp-local — per-toolkit stdio MCP servers for Claude Code / Codex and how they are configured.

params.question: mcp local_cli local_server StdioMCPServer toolkit_server toolkit_config hosts

queries.intent: Orient: the agent daemon (agentd) — JSON-RPC over UDS, MCP stdio proxy, how a caller is identified.

params.question: agentd daemon JSON-RPC unix socket MCP stdio proxy DaemonAgentProxy

queries.intent: Orient: MCP client-side OAuth2 in core (oauth.py, oauth2_storage, oauth2_state) — is there a loopback redirect / local token store precedent for a CLI?

params.question: mcp client oauth2 storage state redirect token store callback

queries.intent: Orient: server-side MCP principal guard and session store — how an MCP caller's principal is established when parrot is the MCP server.

params.question: mcp server principal_guard session_store principal binding

queries.intent: Orient: existing CLI/device-code identity bootstrap and its spec (FEAT-266 O365 homologation) — what 'CLI identity' means today.

params.question: cli identity O365_PRINCIPAL device code bootstrap canonical principal

queries.intent: Read the wiki page of the REPL entry to see where the permission context / user id is built for a CLI-run agent.
Read the wiki page of the mcp-local CLI command (how a toolkit stdio server is launched and what env/config it receives).
Read the wiki page of the toolkit stdio server (tool execution path, permission context, broker).
Read the wiki page of the MCP OAuth2 provider in parrot.auth.oauth2 (what 'mcp' auth_kind means for the broker).
Read the wiki page of the server-side MCP principal guard.
Follow edges from the CLI identity module to find every caller of the O365 bootstrap.
Follow edges from the stdio MCP server to see which modules feed it tools, config and credentials.
Callers of the CLI identity bootstrap — which CLI entry points thread a permission context today.
How the credential principal reaches tools in CLI / stdio paths — usages of the ToolManager credential seam outside tools/manager.py.
Whether the stdio MCP server / toolkit server build or receive a PermissionContext at all.
MCP client-side OAuth precedent: loopback redirect, local token storage classes, callback server for a CLI process.
Where the CredentialBroker is built for non-server surfaces (CLI, stdio MCP, agentd) and what deps it needs.
CLI entry points: registered `parrot` sub-commands and whether any login / auth / token command exists.
How stdio toolkit servers reach secrets / vault today (env, VaultTokenSync, navconfig) — the credential-retrieval seam S-4 must replace with a remote CredentialStore.
How parrot registers stdio servers into Claude Code / Codex host configs (command, args, env) — the channel for passing a CLI principal / token to the server process.
Server-side MCP principal binding and per-session identity (how parrot-as-MCP-server identifies callers; reusable for a CLI session token?).
Whether the device-code provider is O365-specific or a generic device-code engine reusable for other providers from a CLI.
List the agentd package to locate the daemon entry, the UDS server and any auth/identity module.
Existing test coverage for the CLI, mcp-local and agentd surfaces.
Read the REPL entry: where the agent is loaded, where ask() is called and how the permission context / user id is supplied.
Read the mcp-local CLI command: how a stdio server process is launched and configured.
Read the stdio MCP server: tool dispatch, request context, any identity.
Read the toolkit stdio server: how a toolkit is instantiated, how tools execute and where credentials would be injected.
Read the toolkit config model for stdio servers (what can be passed: env, secrets, user).
Read the hosts module: how Claude Code / Codex host configs are written.
Read the MCP client OAuth module: authorization flow driven from the parrot process (redirect handling, token persistence).
Read the MCP OAuth2 token storage backends (candidate precedent for a CLI-side token cache).
Read the MCP OAuth2 config model (redirect URI, flows supported).
Read the MCP auth provider in parrot.auth.oauth2 (auth_kind 'mcp' in the broker).
Read the O365 device-code provider: fail-closed principal, polling loop, vault write — the only CLI-grade flow today.
Read the broker factory: which deps each auth kind requires, to see what a CLI / stdio process must provide.
Read the server-side MCP principal guard header (principal model, how it is derived from the transport).
Read the server-side MCP CLI (parrot-server MCP command surface, auth options).
Read the agentd daemon entry / server module found by Q024 (identity of the UDS caller, MCP stdio proxy).
Read the CLI commands module for any existing auth / login / config subcommand.
Read the CLI session module (what the REPL persists locally — a natural home for a login token).
Read session_identity (server-side identity extraction) to compare with what a CLI could present.
Read the MCP context module (_CREDENTIAL_VAR / ReadonlyContext per-call credential path that S-1 M9 relies on).
Read the expose-toolkits-as-local-mcp spec design section — how credentials for stdio toolkit servers were intended to work.
Read the agent-cli-daemon spec design section — daemon identity / auth model as designed.
Read the S-1 spec's M1 Principal / PrincipalResolver and M8 IdentityPrincipalResolver skeletons — the contract S-4 must implement for the CLI.
Recent history of the CLI package (who touched identity / REPL and why).
Recent history of the local-MCP surface (mcp-local, stdio servers, hosts).
Recent history of agentd.
Recent history of the MCP client-side OAuth files (is the loopback / storage path alive or stale?).
Recent history of the server-side MCP principal guard / session store.

expected_findings: Exactly where a CLI-run agent (REPL, agentd) obtains its user identity today and what it is keyed on (Entra OID/email vs Navigator user_id)
How a parrot mcp-local stdio server is launched, configured and reaches secrets; whether any per-user identity enters it
Whether parrot.mcp already has a CLI-grade OAuth precedent (loopback redirect, local token store) reusable for connect-from-CLI
Whether device-code is a generic engine or O365-only
How the server-side MCP principal guard identifies callers (candidate transport for a CLI login token)
Which broker deps a non-server process must provide, hence what a remote CredentialStore over the server API must replace
Existing tests and recent activity on these surfaces
